**Title:** Same Name, Different Unit: Identifying Source-Specific Units in Web Price Fusion

**Abstract (300 words):**

Aggregators, indexes and oracles combine prices from many web sources and assume that every source's dollar is the same dollar. Often it is not. A crypto exchange's dollar balance is a claim on that exchange, and it can lose value when its banking breaks down. An aggregator then mistakes a change in the dollar for a change in price. We detect this from public prices. When an exchange's dollar moves, every asset there moves by the same amount, so the part of the price gaps that all assets share measures the dollar's offset. A stablecoin traded there, corrected for its price elsewhere, separates a move in the dollar from demand for the assets. We give an identification result, a test and its size and power. Flowerday et al. (2026) proposed that Bitfinex's 2018–19 premium reflected a discount on its dollar but could not test it. From November 2018 to May 2019, once Tether's own price on Kraken was netted out, Bitfinex's Tether price tracked its dollar offset with slope 0.97 (95% interval 0.94 to 1.00). Binance.US in 2023 gave a slope of 1.00, close to mechanical, though a two-stablecoin version of the test rejected. A pre-registered panel of eight currency units gave a pooled slope just below one (0.978, 0.962 to 0.989). On a second venue, Kraken, it was 1.005 (0.867 to 1.289). A plain median was hard to beat in three one-shot fusion tests, but it failed in two pre-registered ones. Where most trading shared one stablecoin that lost its peg, a frozen unit-aware method beat the median, stablecoin conversion and source-reliability weighting (CRH), and narrowly a median of dollar-quoted markets. In six local-currency markets, official-rate conversion erred by about 128.1 bps against 6.8 through the venue's own stablecoin, and so did the median of the officially converted markets.

**Suggested keywords:** exchange dollars; unit of account; truth discovery; price feeds and oracles; Web data quality; cryptocurrency markets; reproducibility
